parts.title: Part 1 · Study routines
prompts: Do you prefer to study in the morning or in the evening?
Where do you usually do your homework?
Do you like learning with other people?
parts.sample: I usually study in the evening because the house is quieter. I use a desk next to my bedroom window. When I have something difficult to practise, I prefer to study with a friend because we can explain our mistakes to each other.

parts.title: Part 2 · A skill you learned
prompts: Describe a useful skill you learned outside school.
Say what it was, when you learned it and who helped you.
Explain how you use it now.
parts.sample: A useful skill I learned outside school was cooking a simple meal. When I moved into a flat with two other students, I did not know how to make much beyond instant noodles. My aunt showed me how to cook rice and make a soup with vegetables and eggs. The difficult part was timing everything. The first time I tried on my own, the rice was still hard when the soup was ready. I started preparing the ingredients before turning on the stove, which made the process much less stressful. Now I cook two or three times a week, and I have enough confidence to change the recipe depending on what is in the fridge. It saves me money, but what I enjoy most is being able to make dinner for someone else when they visit.

parts.title: Part 3 · Learning throughout life
prompts: Why do adults sometimes find it difficult to learn new skills?
Which skills should schools teach alongside academic subjects?
Can online lessons replace practical experience?
parts.sample: An online lesson is useful when someone needs to see a process several times. A learner can pause a video and look closely at a tool, for example. The challenge is that a video cannot always tell you what you are doing wrong. In skills such as cooking or repairing equipment, I would use online lessons to prepare and then ask for feedback on an actual attempt.
